question.text: Under Section 19FA of the Depositories Act, what is the penalty for a depository's failure to conduct business in a fair manner?

answer.text: Not less than one crore rupees but which may extend to ten crore rupees
Not less than ten crore rupees but which may extend to fifty crore rupees
Not less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to one crore rupees
Not less than five crore rupees but which may extend to twenty-five crore rupees or three times the gains, whichever is higher

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 19FA of the Depositories Act, if a depository fails to conduct its business with participants, issuers, or persons associated with the securities markets in a fair manner, it shall be liable to a penalty which shall not be less than five crore rupees but which may extend to twenty-five crore rupees or three times the amount of gains made out of such failure, whichever is higher. The Trap: The "one lakh to one crore" range matches the nearby penalty provisions on pages 229-230 of the workbook for other contraventions, while the "one crore to ten crore" and "ten crore to fifty crore" ranges are plausible but unrelated brackets. Note: Section 19FA is the high-end civil penalty band on these pages, sitting alongside the nearby Rs 1 lakh and Rs 1 crore provisions for other Depositories Act contraventions.
